close_reason: Added ':' to domain guard in fetch_mta_sts_policy_body; added domain_with_port_rejected test
description: The SSRF guard in fetch_mta_sts_policy_body rejects '://', '/', '@', '#', '?', '[', ']' but not ':'. A recipient domain containing ':' (e.g. 'example.com:8080') constructs URL 'https://mta-sts.example.com:8080/.well-known/mta-sts.txt', which attempts connection to port 8080 instead of the standard 443. WebPKI cert validation still applies (the cert must be valid for mta-sts.example.com), so this is a low-risk SSRF, but it allows unexpected port selection. RFC 8461 §3.3 requires the policy URL to use the standard HTTPS port. Fix: add ':' to the domain guard character set.
title: ':' not in fetch_mta_sts_policy_body domain guard — allows non-standard HTTPS port
